config.title: Build typed route config map

intro.title: Build typed route config map
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed route configuration map using TypeScript. You will create a central object that defines your application's routes, where each route has a specific path and associated component type. This teaches you how to use TypeScript's Record utility type and union types to enforce type safety across your route definitions. By the end, you'll have a reusable, error-resistant configuration that helps manage navigation in a structured way.
intro.usecase: Typed route configuration maps are essential in modern web applications where navigation must be predictable and maintainable. In e-commerce platforms like Shopify or Amazon, they ensure product pages, checkout flows, and user dashboards have correct parameters and permissions. Content management systems like WordPress use them to validate admin panel routes and editorial workflows. This pattern prevents broken links and type errors in complex applications with dozens of interconnected views.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript type definition for a route configuration object.
Initialize a typed route configuration map using a Record type.
Manipulate route configuration objects to add new route entries.
Apply type annotations to ensure route parameters are correctly typed.
Integrate the typed route map into a simulated routing structure.
Configure route objects with nested children routes using proper typing.
Update existing route configurations to modify path or component properties.
